reasoning: Under the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, the federal fiscal year begins on October 1, by which point Congress is required to enact all regular appropriations bills (now numbering 12) to fully fund the government on time. According to data from the Congressional Research Service and analyses by organizations such as the Pew Research Center, Congress has enacted all required regular appropriations bills before the start of the fiscal year in only four instances: fiscal years 1977, 1989, 1995, and 1997. Since fiscal year 1997, Congress has consistently relied on continuing resolutions, omnibus spending packages, or enacted appropriations well past the October 1 deadline.
